Differences from Python anndata

Source: vignettes/deviations.Rmd
deviations.Rmd

anndata.claude follows Python anndata 0.13.4. Observable behaviour (values, errors, warnings, printed output and files written) matches Python except where this page says otherwise. Each deviation has a reason and the ticket or decision record it comes from. Tickets are in .scratch/<sub-project>/issues/ and decision records (ADRs) in docs/adr/ of the source repository. Help pages with deviations have a “Deviations from Python” section that links here.

Deviations on disk are rare, because files must round trip with Python. The ones that exist are under “On-disk files”.

Indexing and assignment

  • R indices. Indices are 1-based, negative integers exclude, logical vectors need the full axis length and character vectors match names (first match). Zero, NA, unknown names and mixed signs raise anndata_index_error. Reason: R semantics (roadmap principles, core-object spec “Subsetting”). Help page: ?anndata-index.
  • Mapping keys. Keys of obsm, varm, obsp, varp, layers and uns must be single non-empty strings, because R lists cannot hold NA or empty names. Python accepts any key (core-object/05).
  • Data frames in obsp and varp. A data frame is an error. Python converts a homogeneous one to an array, but the spec allows only matrices (core-object/05).
  • Non-character obs_names in a list. A list of obs with non-character names is coerced to character with an anndata_implicit_modification_warning. Python keeps them (core-object/02).
  • Assigning obs and var. A value without its own names resets the names to "0", "1", … as in Python, and obs_names<- accepts duplicates without a warning (Python warns only at construction), see core-object/07.
  • raw$X and raw$var can be assigned. R keeps validated setters so that adata$raw$var$col <- v works, where Python modifies them in place (core-object/08).

Views

Help page: ?AnnData

  • Accessors return plain R values. In Python x = view.X; x[0, 0] = 1 modifies the View, but in R x <- view$X; x[1, 1] <- 1 only changes x. Assign through the View (view$X[1, 1] <- 1) instead. Reason: R values are copied on modification (ADR 0002 and views spec).
  • Warnings are broader. R cannot tell view$obs$col <- x from view$obs <- x, so setting obs, var, uns or X always makes the View actual with a warning, where Python is silent for some forms (views/03). An item assignment on X, layers or obsm says “Setting element” where Python says “Trying to modify attribute”.
  • Nested values are snapshots. A change to a nested value of uns never reaches the parent, and view$obs$num[1] <- v detaches instead of raising pandas’ ChainedAssignmentError (views/02 and views/03).
  • View of a backed object. view$X[1, 1] <- 5 makes the View actual with a warning, where Python silently changes nothing (backed/05).

Backed mode

  • copy() to the same file twice. Python overwrites the first copy’s open file in "r+" mode but rhdf5 cannot truncate an open file, so R raises an error in both modes (backed/05).
  • Writing a View of a backed object in place. Python writes a corrupt file and fails, R refuses with anndata_invalid_argument_error (backed/05). Moving a backed View’s file fails before anything is moved (anndata_file_not_found_error when the move fails), where Python renames the file first and leaves it corrupt.
  • Writing to an existing file. Writing to a new path that exists truncates it, where Python opens it in append mode and updates it (backed/05).
  • Backed raw (backed/05). Writing a backed raw in place raises anndata_not_supported_error (Python fails with AttributeError), and writing it to a new file works. filename <- NULL keeps the values of raw$X, where Python leaves None. raw$X<- exists in R for nested assignment but is refused on a backed raw.
  • chunked_X() is not a generator. It returns a list of list(chunk, start, end) with 1-based inclusive rows, not a generator with 0-based half-open ranges (backed/06).

Lazy reading

Help pages: ?read_lazy, ?read_elem_lazy and ?lazy-dense

  • uns is read eagerly. Python keeps arrays inside uns as dask arrays (lazy/07).
  • t() of a lazy AnnData stays lazy. It fails with a ValueError in Python, which is a bug there (lazy/07).
  • Lazy frames are indexed by row name. Python’s Dataset2D has no loc (lazy/07).
  • read_elem_lazy() takes a path or handle. R has no element object like h5py’s (lazy/07).
  • An int32 array holding -2^31. NA_integer_ has the same bit pattern, so a lazy seed (whose type is fixed before reading) raises anndata_dtype_overflow_error when such a block is realised, and suggests an eager read (lazy/04).
  • R types. Lazy arrays have DelayedArray’s R types and not the promoted On-disk dtype (concat/06).

Concatenation

Help page: ?concat

  • Lazy obs and var are read into memory. Python keeps them lazy, which loses categorical columns and fails on an outer join with string columns (concat/06).
  • Mixed object columns. Annotation columns that Python would turn into a mixed object column (numbers with strings, bool with numbers) raise anndata_unsupported_value_error. Keys are converted to character (concat/03).

Reading other formats

Help page: ?read_excel

  • read_excel(). Python’s object X (text in the first column) has no R form, so X is numeric. Names are always strings, even with restrict_index_types off (other-formats/07).
  • read_umi_tools(). A row with a missing field raises anndata_invalid_value_error, where Python reads a missing last field as a NaN count (other-formats/05).
  • Complex Matrix Market files. read_mtx() rejects the complex field, where Python silently drops the imaginary part (wontfix, fix_plan.md).
  • Unsupported formats. Loom is not supported (deprecated in Python, roadmap spec), nor are zip stores and writing zarr v2 (NEWS.md).

Reading and writing h5ad

  • Invalid arguments are classed errors. Errors are raised before the file is opened. chunk_size of 0 or less is an error (Python hangs) and as_sparse on a sparse X is anndata_invalid_argument_error (Python gives an AttributeError). The /raw group keeps its Encoding attributes when raw X is written dense (Python drops them) (h5ad-io/11).
  • Old releases. Files from anndata before 0.6 and 0.6.x zarr stores are not supported (legacy-formats spec).

On-disk files

  • NA and NaN. Double NA_real_ and NaN are both written as NaN, and read back as NaN (h5ad-io spec, “Encodings”).
  • Out-of-range sparse indices. Help page: ?h5ad. A CSR or CSC matrix whose indices are out of range for its shape (such as the 1-based indices Illumina DRAGEN 4.5.4 writes) raises anndata_io_registry_error, with a hint when they look 1-based. Python reads such a file without complaint into an invalid scipy matrix (check_format() fails and toarray() misplaces values), and Matrix cannot hold an invalid matrix.
  • Unsorted sparse indices. Unsorted indices of a CSR or CSC matrix are sorted on read, with their data, because Matrix needs them sorted. The matrix is the same but the on-disk order of indices and data can differ (ADR 0006).
  • Compression of rec-arrays. Help page: ?io-rec-array. compression = "lzf" writes an HDF5 rec-array uncompressed, because the compound helper only supports gzip (ADR 0008 and h5ad-io/15).
  • zarr rec-array chunks. A zarr rec-array is written as one chunk, where Python uses zarr’s guess_chunks (zarr-io/14).
  • complex64. Reading complex64 raises a classed error naming the path, because rhdf5 cannot read it (h5ad-io spec, “Encodings”).

See also vignette("anndata-claude") for an overview.
